title: A non-square element cuts a regular local hypersurface
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] and let $f\in\mathfrak m$. If $f\notin\mathfrak m^2$, then $R/fR$ is a regular local ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), used in the proof of More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PF

proof.text: (Setup.) $R$ is a Noetherian local ring and $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $d=\dim R$ elements [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. Then $\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=d$ [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension]. Since $f\in\mathfrak m$ and $f\notin\mathfrak m^2$, the class $\bar f$ of $f$ in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is nonzero; in particular $d\ge1$.

source.place: Algebra, discussion before Definition Tag 00KU (definition-regular-local): 'the minimal number of generators of m equals dim m/m^2'; tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: (Extend $f$ to a regular system of parameters.) The nonzero vector $\bar f$ of the $d$-dimensional $\kappa$-vector space $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ extends to a basis $\bar f,\bar y_2,\dots,\bar y_d$; choose lifts $y_2,\dots,y_d\in\mathfrak m$ and put $x_1=f$, $x_i=y_i$ for $2\le i\le d$. The $R$-module $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated ($R$ is Noetherian, [def-weil-regular-scheme]) and $\mathfrak m\cdot\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m^2$, so $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m\,\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$; as the images of $x_1,\dots,x_d$ span it, Nakayama's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (with $A=R$, $M=\mathfrak m$) shows that $x_1=f,x_2,\dots,x_d$ generate $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular): 'choose x_1,...,x_c in I whose images in m/m^2 are linearly independent and supplement with x_{c+1},...,x_d to get a minimal system of generators of m'; Nakayama, Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $x_1=f,x_2,\dots,x_d$ are $d=\dim R$ elements of $\mathfrak m$ generating $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] with $c=1$, $R/x_1R=R/fR$ is a regular local ring (of dimension $d-1$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PF (lemma-quotient-regular): 'it suffices to prove that f is not in m^2, see Algebra, Lemma 00NQ'; Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM) in algebra.tex
